**Market Parameters Report – January 2009** 





### **1. Demand for platinum** 

- _After a heavy fall in 2008, demand for platinum is expected to decline again in 2009 with buoyant demand in jewellery and retail investment failing to offset significant weakness in autocatalyst and lower demand in glass and electronics.  Some improvement is expected in 2010 as auto production rises from a low base and jewellery further improves._ 

|**Platinum 000 ozs**|**2007**|**2008E**|**2009F**|**2010F**|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Autocatalyst|4,220|3,938|3,360|3,540|
|Jewellery|1,482|942|1,561|1,819|
|_Chemical_|_365_|_373_|_431_|_387_|
|_Electronics_|_461_|_378_|_352_|_358_|
|_Glass_|_402_|_480_|_278_|_282_|
|_Petroleum_|_248_|_218_|_284_|_301_|
|_Other_|_471_|_794_|_635_|_540_|
|Industrial|1,946|2,244|1,980|1,869|
|**Total**|**7,649**|**7,124**|**6,901**|**7,228**|



### **1.1  Autocatalyst** 

- The situation in the auto industry goes from bad to worse, forcing us to again revise our forecast for global vehicle production. With almost every vehicle market now experiencing a sharp downturn, short‐time working and/or assembly line closures are near universal as auto makers battle to shift bloated inventories and avoid haemorrhaging more cash. 

- After a 3% decline in 2008, we now expect a 12% fall in global vehicle production in 2009. The big numbers here are a disastrous 25% drop in North America this year with Europe and Japan expected to fall by 13% and 11% respectively.  China is the only producer of scale with some remaining growth, although at a forecast 1.5% this is somewhat tenuous. 

- The effect on platinum demand is a steep decline in 2009 and a moderate improvement in 2010, when we expect a 9% gain in global vehicle output.  Our rationale for a partia

l recovery in vehicle production 2010 is based on inventory clearances (the focus of 2009) and the effect of pent up demand, especially in North America after heavy production losses in both 2008 and 2009. 

### **1.2 Jewellery** 

- In this report, our forecast for platinum demand in jewellery remains unchanged pending the completion of additional field research in each of the key markets over the coming weeks.  This will focus not only on net demand but also on scrap recycling; a significant feature of the market in 2008, especially over the first six months. 

### **1.3 Industrial** 

- We have made upward revisions to our estimates for retail investment in Japan (included in Other), where lower dollar prices and a strong yen have triggered surging demand.  At the same time we are lowering our estimates for demand in electronics – due to reduced loadings and slower growth in hard drives – and the glass industry, where the pace of expansion in both LCD and fibreglass is slowing considerably.

### **2. Demand for palladium** 

- _With few compensating factors palladium demand in 2009 will suffer the brunt of collapsing vehicle production and deteriorating sales of consumer electronic goods.  Unlike platinum, there is little sign at present of demand from jewellery coming to the rescue, thus postponing a recovery in overall demand until 2010 when vehicle production is expected to improve._ 

|**Palladium 000 ozs**|**2007**|**2008E**|**2009F**|**2010F**|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Autocatalyst|4,923|4,723|4,213|4,782|
|Jewellery|1,025|1,072|1,148|1,247|
|_Dental_|_661_|_623_|_682_|_688_|
|_Chemical_|_383_|_414_|_454_|_491_|
|_Electronics_|_1,275_|_1,313_|_1,182_|_1,300_|
|_Other_|_115_|_106_|_94_|_96_|
|Industrial|2,435|2,457|2,412|2,575|
|**Total**|**8,383**|**8,252**|**7,772**|**8,603**|



### **2.1 Autocatalyst** 

- Broadly speaking, a similar story to that of platinum, with a downward revision to our 2009 forecast flowing from our revised outlook for auto production.  With North America expected to suffer even steeper production losses (the largest of any region) and it being the most intensive user of palladium, the impact on palladium demand is accentuated. 

- However, we see palladium rebounding in 2010 (to 2008 levels) at a rate outperforming our anticipated improvement in vehicle production.  This is due to the beneficial effect of continuing substitution gains in both diesel and gasoline, at the expense of platinum (which suffers the opposite effect). 

### **2.2 Jewellery** 

- As with platinum, we maintain our estimates for palladium demand in jewellery applications pending the results of field research in the key markets over the coming weeks. 

### **2.3 Industrial** 

- The outlook for consumer electronic goods continues to deteriorate with industry analysts now forecasting that 2009 will register the first ever decline in mobile handset shipments, only minimal growth in p

ersonal computer sales and a sharp reduction in display panel volumes.  This comes on top of lower estimates for vehicle production, in which the content of electronic components has risen markedly over recent years.  Accordingly, we have again lowered our estimates for palladium demand in electronic applications. 

- Otherwise, our demand estimates remain unchanged pending a major review as our research cycle for our _Platinum & Palladium Survey_ is completed over the next two months.

**Market Parameters Report – January 2009** 





### **3. Supply** 

### **3.1 Platinum supply** 

- _Our forecast for platinum supply remains unchanged from our previous report in December and captures all announced changes in mine production with some allowance for the possibility of further modest production cuts._ 

|**Platinum 000 ozs**|**2007**|**2008E**|**2009F**|**2010F**|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|**Mineproduction:**|||||
|South Africa|5,075|4,585|4,702|4,928|
|Russia|917|793|770|765|
|Canada|197|218|187|262|
|United States|120|112|108|108|
|Zimbabwe|169|168|180|191|
|Others|97|117|110|112|
|**Total mineproduction**|**6,575**|**5,993**|**6,056**|**6,365**|
|Autocatalyst recycling|926|1,019|1,107|1,208|
|**Total supply**|**7,501**|**7,012**|**7,164**|**7,574**|



- There have been no significant developments since this forecast was updated at the end of December.  We remain of the view that once all of the data for 2008 is available, we will see a further large decline in production; reflecting the impact of power issues over the course of the year, skills shortages, enhanced safety management (much improved over the year) and the Polokwane smelter shut‐down from Early November. 

- With South Africa now soft‐pedalling on expansion, and with production expected to ease elsewhere in the world, global mine output of platinum in 2009 will be almost flat year‐on‐ year, with overall supply receiving only a modest lift from autocatalyst recycling (which we expect will rise again this year). 

- By 2010, it is unlikely South African production will exceed that recorded in 2007; in itself a very dismal year bedevilled by mine‐site fatalities and skills shortages (a long standing issue). In fact, should PGM prices remain near existing levels, the possibility of further production cuts cannot be ruled out.  Some clues on this may emerge during February as the reporting season gets underway.

**Market Parameters Report – January 2009** 





### **3.2 Palladium supply** 

- _As with platinum, our forecasts for platinum supply are unchanged since our previous report in December and capture all announced changes in mine production._ 

|**Palladium 000 ozs**|**2007**|**2008E**|**2009F**|**2010F**|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|**Mineproduction:**|||||
|South Africa|2,676|2,435|2,635|2,809|
|Russia|3,049|2,696|2,523|2,523|
|Canada|557|524|273|357|
|United States|425|376|358|358|
|Zimbabwe|133|130|140|151|
|Others|196|212|214|215|
|**Total mineproduction**

|**7,036**|**6,372**|**6,141**|**6,412**|
|Autocatalyst recycling|963|1,225|1,521|1,845|
|**Total supply**|**7,998**|**7,597**|**7,662**|**8,257**|



- With lower production from both Russia and South Africa, palladium’s mine production profile is expected to track platinum quite closely, with a deep trough in 2008 and 2009 followed by an improvement in 2010. 

- For the time being, we maintain our estimates for palladium recovery (and platinum) from autocatalyst recycling.  This is despite volumes having eased over the second half of 2008 (after a record first half performance) and especially over recent weeks.  We believe this has more to do with lower PGM (and steel) prices than a decline in the flow of scrapped vehicles as sales of new models slump.  Most likely, unprocessed inventories of scrapped autocatalyst are being allowed to accumulate at the beginning of the supply‐chain in the hope of higher prices.  This has occurred many times in the past (although not in recent years) and has generally proven to be short‐term. 

- Aside from these issues, the longer term growth of autocatalyst recycling is assured by finite vehicle life‐spans and the historical fitment rates of autocatalysts and their PGM loadings. Although fully mature, the US recycling market (the largest) will continue to yield increasing volumes of palladium over the next few years (reflecting peak usage in the late 1990s) and Europe (a later adopter of autocatalyst technology) will continue to yield growing amounts of both platinum and palladium from scrapped autocatalysts as it continues its advance towards maturity.

### **4. Market balances** 

### **4.1 Platinum** 

- _With supplies unchanged and revised forecasts for demand, we estimate a relatively modest ”gross deficit” for platinum in 2008 and surpluses at the gross level in both 2009 and 2010._ 

- _Investors in platinum ETFs added a net 102,000 ounces to their holdings in 2008 and we believe similar additions are possible in 2009, assuming moderate prices.  Although the inclusion of this activity implies a tighter market, this is not relevant to platinum’s underlying fundamentals or the scale of above‐ground stocks._ 

|**Platinum 000 ozs**|**2007**|**2008E**|**2009F**|**2010F**|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|New supply|7,501|7,012|7,164|7,574|
|Fabrication demand|7,649|7,124|6,901|7,228|
|**_Gross surplus(deficit)_**|**(149)**|**(113)**|**263**|**345**|
|ETF demand|(194)|(102)|(100)|(50)|
|**Residual surplus(deficit)**|**(343)**|**(215)**|**163**|**295**|



### **4.2 Palladium** 

- _Despite reduced demand estimates, palladium remains in deficit at the “gross level”. However, this is less pronounced than our previous forecast in December suggested and is due to significantly reduced demand from the auto sector._ 

- _Our estimate for sales of palladium from Russian government stocks in 2008 has been increased following heavy shipments into Switzerland in Augu

st/September 2008 and a further large reported delivery into the United States in November.  Although negative for prices, these sales have no effect on the totality of global above‐ground palladium stocks._ 

- _Investors in palladium ETFs added 381,000 ounces to their holdings in 2008.  We anticipate continuing additions in 2009 and 2010, although the pace is likely to be slower.  The net effect this, together with higher Russian stock sales and ongoing gross deficits, is a continuing residual surplus for palladium, especially so in 2009._

|---|---|---|---|---|

|Russia stock sales|900|1,280|1,000|750|
|ETF demand|(280)|(381)|(100)|(100)|
|**Residual surplus(deficit)**|**235**|**244**|**790**|**304**|

**5. Above‐ground stocks** 

- _Above‐ground stocks are implied from historical trade data for Switzerland (dating from 1970) and declared stocks on the Nymex and Tocom futures exchanges.  Excluded are stocks held by governments (including Russia), producers, refiners and fabricators and consumers._ 

|**Implied stocks**|**2007**|**2008E**|**2009F**|**2010F**|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|**Platinum:**|||||
|Stock atyear end(million ozs)|1.45|1.34|1.60|1.95|
|Demand cover(months)|2.3|2.3|2.8|3.2|
|**Palladium:**|||||
|Stock atyear end(million ozs)|8.31|7.66|7.55|7.20|
|Demand cover(months)|12.0|10.6|9.8|8.8|



- Our revised demand estimates (and consequent changes to gross surplus/(deficit) levels) have had little effect on platinum’s forecast above‐ground stocks, with demand cover remaining close to 3 months. 

- Similarly, the effect on palladium is also relatively minor.  Above‐ground stocks are expected to remain substantial and will continue to represent a little over 7 months demand cover over the duration of this forecast. 

- _Note: flows of palladium from Russian state stocks into Zurich have been excluded from the forecast years 2008, 2009 and 2010 (although these are known to have occurred already this year).  While these movements may cause Zurich stocks to rise, we have taken the view this will be matched by a corresponding decline in Russia’s holdings._

**Market Parameters Report – January 2009** 





### **6. Prices and related indicators** 

### **6.1 Platinum** 

_Platinum appears comfortable above $900, aided by stronger gold prices.  Volatility has eased significantly._ 

_Platinum’s RSI has levelled off over January and remains slightly positive.  This is a good sign and implies platinum would not be regarded as over‐ bought at recent price levels by technically based traders._ 

_The cross‐over of spot and the 50 day MA in early January may have contributed to platinum’s more positive tone.  The next challenge is getting to a cross‐ over with

the 200 day MA; this remains some distance off._ 







Page | 7 

**Market Parameters Report – January 2009** 





### **6.2 Palladium** 

_A firmer tone for palladium in January with volatility easing as prices levelled off near $190 towards month end._ 

_Somewhat firmer prices and nothing in the RSI to suggest palladium might be viewed as over‐bought.  Perhaps palladium can now consolidate support around $190; aided by better gold and platinum prices._ 

_Palladium’s moving averages are similar to platinum, with the 50 day average well below the 200 day and a long wait in store for the next crossover.  The 50 day MA and spot have reached convergence._
